A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. For M-dominant κ the corresponding H³_w vanishes unless w=w₃.

items.name: Cuspidal ordinary completed amplitude
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. Before residual localization the ordinary cusp Verma completed complex is supported in degrees1,…,3.

items.name: Cuspidal ordinary filtration before localization
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. Its degree3 graded pieces are coker(H¹_{w₂}(−D)→H³_{w₃}(−D)), H²_{w₂}(−D), H¹_{w₁}(−D), H⁰_{w₀}(−D); degree2 has H²_{w₃}(−D) and the kernel of that map; degree1 is H¹_{w₃}(−D).

items.name: Noncuspidal ordinary completed amplitude
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. Before localization the noncuspidal ordinary Verma complex is supported in degrees3,…,5.

items.name: Noncuspidal ordinary filtration before localization
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. Degree3 has H³_{w₃},H²_{w₂},H¹_{w₁},ker(H⁰_{w₀}→H²_{w₁}); degree4 has that map's cokernel and H¹_{w₀}; degree5 has H²_{w₀}.

items.name: Non-Eisenstein boundary vanishing
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. At the irreducible residual maximal ideal, the map from cusp to ordinary completed cohomology is an isomorphism. This uses the source-qualified boundary theorem of Newton–Thorne, not genericity alone.

items.name: Bruhat coefficient boundary vanishing
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. At the same residual ideal, cusp-to-noncusp ordinary big cohomology is an isomorphism on every Bruhat piece.

items.name: Ordinary degree-zero boundary is Eisenstein
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. The degree-zero boundary of the higher-Hida complex vanishes at this residual ideal, using normalization of the ordinary Igusa boundary and the GL2/GSp4 Hecke comparison.

items.name: Localized ordinary middle-degree concentration
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. At the irreducible residual ideal, the ordinary Verma/Borel completed complex is concentrated in degree3.

items.name: Four-piece ordinary filtration
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. Its degree3 cohomology after C_p extension has Gr^j=H^j_{w_j}, j=0,…,3, with the specified big coefficient and B-character twist.

items.name: Sen eigenvalues on ordinary pieces
items.statement: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial. On Gr^3,Gr^2,Gr^1,Gr^0 respectively, the Sen eigenvalues are (−λ₁−λ₂−w)/2,(−2+λ₁−λ₂−w)/2,(−4+λ₂−λ₁−w)/2,(−6+λ₁+λ₂−w)/2.

items.name: Classical singular-weight support
items.statement: Set λ=(1,1;w) for even w and retain the irreducible residual localization. Let V be degree3 ordinary Borel completed cohomology, with the four Bruhat pieces and their character twists. Set a=−1−w/2 and b=−2−w/2. Ordinary classical ω^{(1,1;−w)} cohomology is supported on the union of the length2 and length3 Bruhat strata.

items.name: Classical singular Cousin complex
items.statement: Set λ=(1,1;w) for even w and retain the irreducible residual localization. Let V be degree3 ordinary Borel completed cohomology, with the four Bruhat pieces and their character twists. Set a=−1−w/2 and b=−2−w/2. That cohomology is represented by H²_{w₂}(ω^{(1,1;−w)})→H³_{w₃}(ω^{(1,1;−w)}) in degrees2 and3, with differential the geometric Cousin boundary.

items.name: Classical-to-big singular comparison
items.statement: Set λ=(1,1;w) for even w and retain the irreducible residual localization. Let V be degree3 ordinary Borel completed cohomology, with the four Bruhat pieces and their character twists. Set a=−1−w/2 and b=−2−w/2. The classical-to-big maps on these two supported ordinary terms are isomorphisms, by the rank-one BGG sequence and the slope exclusion of its kernel.

items.name: Generalized Sen eigenspace extension
items.statement: Set λ=(1,1;w) for even w and retain the irreducible residual localization. Let V be degree3 ordinary Borel completed cohomology, with the four Bruhat pieces and their character twists. Set a=−1−w/2 and b=−2−w/2. The generalized a eigenspace V[(Θ−a)²] is an extension of Gr² by Gr³, with Θ−a inducing a map Gr²→Gr³; similarly the generalized b eigenspace uses Gr⁰ and Gr¹.

items.name: Sen operator and Cousin boundary
items.statement: Set λ=(1,1;w) for even w and retain the irreducible residual localization. Let V be degree3 ordinary Borel completed cohomology, with the four Bruhat pieces and their character twists. Set a=−1−w/2 and b=−2−w/2. Under the classical/big identifications, the map Gr²→Gr³ induced by Θ−a is a NONZERO scalar multiple of the classical Cousin differential. Its source proof imports the unresolved constrained-fibre comparison3.6.15 through3.6.9.

items.name: Minuscule GSp4 semisimplicity criterion
items.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite and enlarge coefficients as needed. Continuous G_Q-representations are unramified outside finitely many primes. Polynomial-annihilation conditions below are required on a density-one set of unramified Frobenius classes, not merely equality of traces. If ρ:G_Q→GSp4(E-bar) has Zariski closure containing Sp4 and every characteristic polynomial of ρ(Frob_ℓ) annihilates s(Frob_ℓ), then the finite-dimensional representation s is a direct sum of copies of ρ.

items.name: Induced symplectic semisimplicity criterion
items.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite and enlarge coefficients as needed. Continuous G_Q-representations are unramified outside finitely many primes. Polynomial-annihilation conditions below are required on a density-one set of unramified Frobenius classes, not merely equality of traces. The same conclusion holds if ρ is irreducible, restricts to ϱ⊕ϱ^c over an index-two subgroup G_E, and its Zariski closure contains SL2×SL2. The mixed-extension proof uses reciprocal eigenvalues λ,λ⁻¹ on the determinant−1 component of O4.

items.name: Galois representation of an ordinary overconvergent form
items.statement: Let f be an ordinary overconvergent GSp4 eigenform of coherent weight (2,2;−w), w even, with smooth torus eigencharacter χ_f and maximal ideal m_f. Its Hecke polynomial is P_ℓ, for geometric Frobenius, so the interpolated representation is normalized as ρ_π∨ε⁻³. Let λ=(1,1;w), and V=H³ of the ordinary Borel completed complex localized at m_{ρ̄_f}. There is a continuous semisimple ρ_f:G_Q→GSp4(Q_p-bar), unramified outside the prescribed S, whose Frobenius polynomial away from S is P_ℓ modulo m_f.

items.name: Ordinary local characters of the interpolated representation
items.statement: Let f be an ordinary overconvergent GSp4 eigenform of coherent weight (2,2;−w), w even, with smooth torus eigencharacter χ_f and maximal ideal m_f. Its Hecke polynomial is P_ℓ, for geometric Frobenius, so the interpolated representation is normalized as ρ_π∨ε⁻³. Let λ=(1,1;w), and V=H³ of the ordinary Borel completed complex localized at m_{ρ̄_f}. The local representation is Borel-valued with diagonal characters χ₄⁻¹z^{−1−w/2},χ₃⁻¹z^{−1−w/2},χ₂⁻¹z^{−2−w/2},χ₁⁻¹z^{−2−w/2} under local reciprocity, including evaluation at p. Remove the duplicated inverses in the printed last two entries.

items.name: Isotypic completed eigenspace
items.statement: Let f be an ordinary overconvergent GSp4 eigenform of coherent weight (2,2;−w), w even, with smooth torus eigencharacter χ_f and maximal ideal m_f. Its Hecke polynomial is P_ℓ, for geometric Frobenius, so the interpolated representation is normalized as ρ_π∨ε⁻³. Let λ=(1,1;w), and V=H³ of the ordinary Borel completed complex localized at m_{ρ̄_f}. Assume ρ̄_f irreducible and either Sp4 Zariski image or the induced SL2×SL2 hypothesis of4.11.2. Then V[m_f]≅ρ_f⊗W with W finite-dimensional and nonzero, using finite-slope control and Frobenius polynomial annihilation.

items.name: Balanced-multiplicity classicality
items.statement: Let f be an ordinary overconvergent GSp4 eigenform of coherent weight (2,2;−w), w even, with smooth torus eigencharacter χ_f and maximal ideal m_f. Its Hecke polynomial is P_ℓ, for geometric Frobenius, so the interpolated representation is normalized as ρ_π∨ε⁻³. Let λ=(1,1;w), and V=H³ of the ordinary Borel completed complex localized at m_{ρ̄_f}. Assume those image hypotheses, ρ_f locally de Rham, ρ̄_f irreducible, and an integer n with dim_Cp Gr^i(V⊗C_p)[m_f]=n for every i=0,…,3 and dim_Qpbar V[m_f]=4n. Then f is classical. These are eigenspace dimensions; exactness of the eigenspace functor is not an assumption one may omit or infer without the balance.

items.name: Polarized general linear group
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. Define the disconnected group scheme G_n with the displayed semidirect multiplication, identity component and multiplier, including its congruence kernel over a local coefficient ring.
unitTests: GL₁ conjugation is not redundant in characteristic2

items.name: Polarized representation
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. An absolutely irreducible ρ:G_F→GL_n(k) is polarized by μ:G_F⁺→k× if it has a perfect pairing with ⟨ρ(g)x,ρ(cgc)y⟩=μ(g)⟨x,y⟩ and ⟨x,y⟩=−μ(c)⟨y,x⟩.
unitTests: a multiplier alone does not choose a compatible polarization
items.note: The named stage already states this object/interface. BCGP25 is an additional source/application; this classification does not claim implementation.

items.name: Extension of a polarized representation
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. Such a polarized pair extends to r:G_F⁺→G_n(k) with preimage of the identity component G_F and multiplier μ; the extension is unique up to G_n⁰-conjugacy in the stated absolutely irreducible setting.

items.name: Symplectic group with sign
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. On GSp_{2m}×{±1} define the multiplier to be the symplectic multiplier on the first factor, ignoring the sign factor.
unitTests: do not multiply the multiplier by the sign

items.name: Symplectic-to-unitary group embedding
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. For standard J, the source explicit map sends (g,+1) to (g,νg) and (g,−1) to (g,νg)(J⁻¹,−1)j; it embeds GSp_{2m}×{±1} into G_{2m} preserving the specified multiplier.

items.name: CM polarization of a symplectic representation
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. Combine a symplectic G_F⁺ representation with the CM quotient sign and the preceding embedding to obtain a polarized G_{2m} representation with unchanged multiplier and identity-component preimage G_F.

items.name: Strong residual oddness
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. In characteristic2 the polarized pair is strongly residually odd at a real place v if r(c_v) is GL_n(k)-conjugate to (I,1)j. This is stronger than the multiplier condition μ(c_v)=1.
unitTests: identity symplectic involution is not automatically strong
an alternating symmetric form fails the nonalternating test

items.name: Strong oddness through symplectic involutions
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. For a symplectic involution A over perfect k of characteristic2, its polarized image is strongly odd precisely when the associated nonsingular symmetric form AJ is nonalternating; classify the congruence forms before applying this criterion.

items.name: Rank classification of strong involutions
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. With r=rank(A−1), odd r is strongly odd; for positive even r the strong class is the one with nonalternating residual symmetric form. The other class and the identity are not strong.

items.name: Strong involutions under Sp4(F2)=S6
items.statement: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1. In the paper S6 identification, transpositions and double transpositions are strongly odd, whereas triple transpositions are not.

items.name: Trace detection and semisimple span
items.statement: Let V=k^n for a subfield k⊂F₂-bar and finite H⊂GL(V), with ad=End_k(V) carrying conjugation and ad⁰=ker(trace). All group-cohomology coefficients and trace projectors below use this characteristic2 representation. The semisimple elements span End(V) exactly when every simple submodule W of ad (equivalently the source ad⁰ test) has some eigenprojector e_{σ,α} for semisimple σ with nonzero trace pairing on W.

items.name: Weak adequacy
items.statement: Let V=k^n for a subfield k⊂F₂-bar and finite H⊂GL(V), with ad=End_k(V) carrying conjugation and ad⁰=ker(trace). All group-cohomology coefficients and trace projectors below use this characteristic2 representation. H is weakly adequate if its semisimple elements span End_k(V); equivalently use the preceding trace-detection criterion. In particular this implies absolute irreducibility.
unitTests: absolute irreducibility alone is not the definition

items.name: Near adequacy
items.statement: Let V=k^n for a subfield k⊂F₂-bar and finite H⊂GL(V), with ad=End_k(V) carrying conjugation and ad⁰=ker(trace). All group-cohomology coefficients and trace projectors below use this characteristic2 representation. H is nearly adequate if it is weakly adequate, H¹(H,k)=0 and H¹(H,ad)=0. For a representation, apply this predicate to its finite image.
unitTests: H¹(ad/k)=0 is a stronger different input when2 divides n

items.name: Polarized local deformation problem
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. A local problem is a subfunctor of fixed-multiplier framed lifts over CNL_{Λ_v}, stable under the congruence kernel of G_n and satisfying the source deformation-condition axioms.
unitTests: GL_n conjugacy alone omits a scalar direction

items.name: Polarized global deformation problem
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. The tuple of F,r̄,O,χ,S,Λ_v and local conditions defines global lifts modulo strict congruence G_n-conjugacy; retain the multiplier and identity-component preimage in families.
unitTests: replacing G_F⁺ by G_F loses the real conditions
items.note: The named stage already states this object/interface. BCGP25 is an additional source/application; this classification does not claim implementation.

items.name: Representing and framed global rings
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. Construct R_S and its T-framed version for nonempty T containing all nontrivial coefficient places; framing is formally smooth of relative dimension (n²+1)#T−1 over the unframed ring.

items.name: Extra polarized tangent direction
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. Let μ_v=ker(H¹(G_{F_v⁺},ad)→H¹(G_{F_v⁺},Lie G_n)); it is the image of the connecting map from k for 0→ad→Lie G_n→k→0.
unitTests: strongly odd real place gives dimension1
the exact sequence need not split integrally at2

items.name: Relative polarized deformation complex
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. Form the mapping-fibre complex imposing local tangent conditions outside T and framing conditions on T; for degrees≥3 its local summands use C^{i−1}(F_v⁺,ad), correcting the cited Thorne typo.

items.name: Dyadic polarized dual Selmer group
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. Define H¹_{S⊥,T} as the kernel of global H¹(ad(1)) to local quotients by μ_v⊥ at T and L_v⊥ outside T, under local Tate trace duality.
unitTests: discarding μ_v changes the dyadic Selmer problem

items.name: Polarized deformation presentation
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. For T nonempty the relative complex has the tangent/obstruction groups in degrees1,2, h²=h¹_{S⊥,T}, and a local-ring power-series presentation with the resulting tangent and relation bounds.

items.name: Dyadic Taylor–Wiles block condition
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. At a split unramified auxiliary place choose an eigenvalue α of semisimple residual Frobenius and its generalized α-block A; lifts have the complementary block unramified and inertia scalar on A via the universal character of the2-primary residue units.
unitTests: forcing every block scalar imposes a different condition

items.name: Dyadic Taylor–Wiles datum
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. A level-N datum is a finite set Q of such split places with q_v≡1 mod2^N, choices α_v and local block conditions; Δ_Q is the product of2-primary residue-unit groups.
unitTests: the primes must also avoid S

items.name: Unavoidable dyadic dual-Selmer class
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. The first real cyclotomic quadratic extension outside F⁺ supplies a nonzero scalar dual-Selmer class, and every allowed Taylor–Wiles datum leaves it unremoved. Choose K_m⁺ not contained in F⁺ with K_{m−1}⁺ contained in F⁺; the printed reverse containment is false.

items.name: Trace detection of a restricted cocycle
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. Under near adequacy, a nonzero relevant class restricted to the cyclotomic field remains nonzero after restriction to the field cut out by ad r̄; semisimple eigenprojector detection then produces the needed Chebotarev value.

items.name: Near-adequate auxiliary primes
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F. Assume additionally F=F⁺(i), unrestricted real conditions with χ(c_v)=−1, near adequacy of ρ̄(G_F), and strong oddness at some real place if n is even. Set T=S\S_∞, q=h¹_{S⊥,T}−1 and g=q+#T−1−[F⁺:Q]n(n−1)/2. For every N there are infinitely many level-N data with #Q=q and R_loc[[X₁,…,X_g]] surjecting onto R^T_{S_Q}.

items.name: Uniform potentially unipotent ramification
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. At a place away from2 there is a single finite local extension on which every lift of the fixed residual representation has unipotent inertia, using finiteness of deformation-ring components and constancy of inertial types.

items.name: Uniformly unramified regular residual lifts
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. If q_v≡1 mod2 and residual Frobenius is unramified regular semisimple, every lift is a sum of characters; a uniform finite local extension makes all lifts unramified.

items.name: Prescribed inertial characteristic polynomial
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. For finite-order characters χ_{v,j} congruent to1, impose det(X−ρ(σ))=∏_j(X−χ_{v,j}(Art_v(σ))⁻¹) for σ in inertia; define the source reduced flat local ring with this condition.
unitTests: an unbound index i/j does not define a condition

items.name: Unipotent-type local components
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. For trivial residual representation and all χ_{v,j}=1 in the source q_v≡1 mod2 setting, each component has dimension n²+1, every special-fibre minimal prime lifts to a unique generic minimal prime, and the generic points have characteristic zero.

items.name: Distinct-inertia local irreducibility
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. For pairwise distinct χ_{v,j} in that setting the type deformation ring is irreducible of dimension n²+1.

items.name: Ordinary GLn local ring
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. There is a reduced2-torsion-free ordinary local ring R_v△ over Λ_{GL_n,v}, represented by the appropriate scheme image of the stable full-flag incidence space.

items.name: Ordinary GLn integral points
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. For every finite E'/E and weight-algebra map to O_E', a framed lift factors through R_v△ exactly when it is upper triangular with ordered inertia characters equal to the corresponding universal character components.

items.name: Large-degree ordinary components
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. If the residual representation is trivial and [F_v⁺:Q₂]>n(n−1)/2+1, then for each minimal prime Q of Λ_{GL_n,v}, R_v△/Q is geometrically irreducible of dimension [F_v⁺:Q₂]n(n+1)/2+n²+1 and its mod-uniformizer fibre is generically reduced.

items.name: Flatness of the flag scheme image
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. Under that local degree hypothesis the ordinary flag incidence scheme image is already flat, so taking an additional flat closure does not alter the GLn ring used here.

items.name: Ordinary algebraic weight
items.statement: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}. A representation is ordinary of weight λ if it has a full stable flag with rank-one quotients whose characters on sufficiently small units α are ∏_ττ(α)^{−(λ_{τ,n−i+1}+i−1)} for the ith quotient.
unitTests: tensoring only over places misses ramified-field embeddings

items.name: Definite unitary integral model
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, every2-adic place split, n≥2 and n[F⁺:Q] divisible by4. Let G be the definite unitary group compact at infinity and quasi-split at finite places, identified with GL_n at split places. Fix the source tame level U, ordinary p-levels and a non-Eisenstein residual automorphic maximal ideal m. Construct this unitary group and its split finite-place integral identifications, using the parity condition and local invariants.

items.name: Definite unitary algebraic forms
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, every2-adic place split, n≥2 and n[F⁺:Q] divisible by4. Let G be the definite unitary group compact at infinity and quasi-split at finite places, identified with GL_n at split places. Fix the source tame level U, ordinary p-levels and a non-Eisenstein residual automorphic maximal ideal m. S_λ(U,O) consists of functions on G(F⁺)\G(A_F⁺^∞) transforming under U by the algebraic coefficient M_λ, tensor-indexed by embeddings of the2-adic fields, with any prescribed Iwahori character factors.
unitTests: places and embeddings are not interchangeable

items.name: Sufficiently small unitary level
items.statement: For the definite unitary group G/F⁺ of §5.7, a compact open U⊂G(A_F⁺^∞) is sufficiently small if, for some finite place v, its projection to G(F⁺_v) has no nonidentity finite-order element. This makes every arithmetic double-quotient stabilizer trivial.
unitTests: ordinary Iwahori level alone need not be small

items.name: Ordinary unitary Hecke algebra
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, every2-adic place split, n≥2 and n[F⁺:Q] divisible by4. Let G be the definite unitary group compact at infinity and quasi-split at finite places, identified with GL_n at split places. Fix the source tame level U, ordinary p-levels and a non-Eisenstein residual automorphic maximal ideal m. Generate the Hecke algebra by unramified double cosets, normalized2-adic U operators and diamonds on the ordinary projector e=lim U^{r!}; the weight-algebra action includes the factor ∏_{τ,i}τ(u_i)^{1−i}.
unitTests: unnormalized U changes the weight specialization

items.name: Ordinary unitary weight control
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, every2-adic place split, n≥2 and n[F⁺:Q] divisible by4. Let G be the definite unitary group compact at infinity and quasi-split at finite places, identified with GL_n at split places. Fix the source tame level U, ordinary p-levels and a non-Eisenstein residual automorphic maximal ideal m. The ordinary Hecke algebra is finite over Λ, reduced, and has Zariski-dense algebraic ordinary specializations with the source control isomorphism.

items.name: Ordinary global dimension lower bound
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, every2-adic place split, n≥2 and n[F⁺:Q] divisible by4. Let G be the definite unitary group compact at infinity and quasi-split at finite places, identified with GL_n at split places. Fix the source tame level U, ordinary p-levels and a non-Eisenstein residual automorphic maximal ideal m. For the source global ordinary problem S_χ attached to the residual ordinary RACSDC seed, dim R_{S_χ}≥dim Λ=1+[F⁺:Q]n. The printed [F:Q] in the weight dimension is incorrect.

items.name: Unitary Galois-to-Hecke map
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, every2-adic place split, n≥2 and n[F⁺:Q] divisible by4. Let G be the definite unitary group compact at infinity and quasi-split at finite places, identified with GL_n at split places. Fix the source tame level U, ordinary p-levels and a non-Eisenstein residual automorphic maximal ideal m. The ordinary Galois representation attached to the localized Hecke algebra gives a surjection R_{S_χ}→T with unramified polynomial ∑_{j=0}^n(−1)^j q_v^{j(j−1)/2}T_v^{(j)}X^{n−j}.

items.name: Unrestricted-away-two ordinary deformation ring
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, every2-adic place split, n≥2 and n[F⁺:Q] divisible by4. Let G be the definite unitary group compact at infinity and quasi-split at finite places, identified with GL_n at split places. Fix the source tame level U, ordinary p-levels and a non-Eisenstein residual automorphic maximal ideal m. R^{T,ord} uses the ordinary conditions at2 and unrestricted conditions at the other places of T, with fixed multiplier ε^{1−n}δ_{F/F⁺}^n and the prescribed residual representation.
api: natural map to the Hecke algebra
unitTests: T contains2 and all seed ramification
this notation is not the T-framed ring

items.name: Uniform local fixed vectors
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, every2-adic place split, n≥2 and n[F⁺:Q] divisible by4. Let G be the definite unitary group compact at infinity and quasi-split at finite places, identified with GL_n at split places. Fix the source tame level U, ordinary p-levels and a non-Eisenstein residual automorphic maximal ideal m. At every place away from2 there is a uniform compact-open depth admitting fixed vectors for all relevant automorphic representations with the fixed residual Galois representation, via the uniform potential-ramification bound and local Langlands.

items.name: Sufficiently deep ordinary tame level
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, every2-adic place split, n≥2 and n[F⁺:Q] divisible by4. Let G be the definite unitary group compact at infinity and quasi-split at finite places, identified with GL_n at split places. Fix the source tame level U, ordinary p-levels and a non-Eisenstein residual automorphic maximal ideal m. At v away from2 choose U_v contained in the uniform fixed-vector subgroup of5.7.12 for the residual local representation. This is the depth hypothesis in the reduced R=T statement.
unitTests: a subgroup of a valid level
a single lift's conductor does not prove uniform depth

items.name: Dyadic near-adequate ordinary finiteness
items.statement: Let n≥2, F CM and ρ̄:G_F→GL_n(F₂-bar) continuous. Assume an ordinary RACSDC GL_n/F form π has r̄_{π,2}≅ρ̄; F/F⁺ is everywhere unramified; all places above2 and all places under ramified π split in F; n[F⁺:Q]≡0 mod4; ρ̄(G_F) is nearly adequate and contains a regular semisimple element; if n is even, the polarized pair (ρ̄,ε̄^{1−n}δ_{F/F⁺}^n) is strongly residually odd at some real place. Let T be a finite set of split finite places of F⁺ containing the2-adic and seed ramified places. Use the ordinary weight algebra Λ and fixed-multiplier global problem of5.7.11. Then R^{T,ord} is finite over Λ.

items.name: Dyadic ordinary reduced R=T
items.statement: Let n≥2, F CM and ρ̄:G_F→GL_n(F₂-bar) continuous. Assume an ordinary RACSDC GL_n/F form π has r̄_{π,2}≅ρ̄; F/F⁺ is everywhere unramified; all places above2 and all places under ramified π split in F; n[F⁺:Q]≡0 mod4; ρ̄(G_F) is nearly adequate and contains a regular semisimple element; if n is even, the polarized pair (ρ̄,ε̄^{1−n}δ_{F/F⁺}^n) is strongly residually odd at some real place. Let T be a finite set of split finite places of F⁺ containing the2-adic and seed ramified places. Use the ordinary weight algebra Λ and fixed-multiplier global problem of5.7.11. If each U_v for v∈T away from2 is sufficiently deep in Definition5.7.13, the map R^{T,ord}→T^{T,ord}(U(l^∞))_m has nilpotent kernel and induces (R^{T,ord})_red≅T^{T,ord}(U(l^∞))_m.

items.name: Two-type ordinary patching system
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, every2-adic place split, n≥2 and n[F⁺:Q] divisible by4. Let G be the definite unitary group compact at infinity and quasi-split at finite places, identified with GL_n at split places. Fix the source tame level U, ordinary p-levels and a non-Eisenstein residual automorphic maximal ideal m. After the prescribed solvable base changes, patch the χ-distinct and unipotent local-type modules over the common ordinary weight algebra, with congruent mod-uniformizer modules, framed dimensions and auxiliary eigenblocks kept compatible.

items.name: Component support by Ihara avoidance
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, every2-adic place split, n≥2 and n[F⁺:Q] divisible by4. Let G be the definite unitary group compact at infinity and quasi-split at finite places, identified with GL_n at split places. Fix the source tame level U, ordinary p-levels and a non-Eisenstein residual automorphic maximal ideal m. The patched distinct-type maximal Cohen–Macaulay module and unique generic lifts of special-fibre components transfer support to the chosen unipotent-type components; retain the automorphic auxiliary-prime component choice.

items.name: Removal of the sacrificial prime
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, every2-adic place split, n≥2 and n[F⁺:Q] divisible by4. Let G be the definite unitary group compact at infinity and quasi-split at finite places, identified with GL_n at split places. Fix the source tame level U, ordinary p-levels and a non-Eisenstein residual automorphic maximal ideal m. Use uniform potential unramifiedness, a second auxiliary neat prime and solvable ordinary descent to remove the first auxiliary level, preserving all local components needed for the reduced R=T theorem.

items.name: Fixed-similitude local lift
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real and ρ̄:G_{F⁺,S}→GSp4(k) absolutely irreducible of multiplier ε̄⁻¹. Let O be the coefficient DVR, Λ_v local coefficient rings and Λ their completed tensor product. Unlike §5, ad=Lie GSp4 has dimension11 and ad⁰=Lie Sp4 has dimension10. Strict equivalence uses the congruence kernel of GSp4, with fixed multiplier ε⁻¹. A lift over A∈CNL_{Λ_v} is a continuous G_{F_v⁺}→GSp4(A) homomorphism reducing to ρ̄ and with multiplier ε⁻¹.
unitTests: a GL4 lift without a pairing is insufficient
items.note: The named stage already states this object/interface. BCGP25 is an additional source/application; this classification does not claim implementation.

items.name: Symplectic local deformation condition
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real and ρ̄:G_{F⁺,S}→GSp4(k) absolutely irreducible of multiplier ε̄⁻¹. Let O be the coefficient DVR, Λ_v local coefficient rings and Λ their completed tensor product. Unlike §5, ad=Lie GSp4 has dimension11 and ad⁰=Lie Sp4 has dimension10. Strict equivalence uses the congruence kernel of GSp4, with fixed multiplier ε⁻¹. A local condition is a quotient-represented subfunctor of the fixed-similitude framed lifts stable under congruence GSp4-conjugacy.
unitTests: an arbitrary set of characteristic-zero points need not define a quotient functor
items.note: The named stage already states this object/interface. BCGP25 is an additional source/application; this classification does not claim implementation.

items.name: Symplectic global deformation problem
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real and ρ̄:G_{F⁺,S}→GSp4(k) absolutely irreducible of multiplier ε̄⁻¹. Let O be the coefficient DVR, Λ_v local coefficient rings and Λ their completed tensor product. Unlike §5, ad=Lie GSp4 has dimension11 and ad⁰=Lie Sp4 has dimension10. Strict equivalence uses the congruence kernel of GSp4, with fixed multiplier ε⁻¹. The residual representation, finite ramification set S, coefficient rings and local conditions define a global strict deformation functor and its T-framed variant.
unitTests: the real-field Galois domain is G_F⁺
items.note: The named stage already states this object/interface. BCGP25 is an additional source/application; this classification does not claim implementation.

items.name: Symplectic framing algebra
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real and ρ̄:G_{F⁺,S}→GSp4(k) absolutely irreducible of multiplier ε̄⁻¹. Let O be the coefficient DVR, Λ_v local coefficient rings and Λ their completed tensor product. Unlike §5, ad=Lie GSp4 has dimension11 and ad⁰=Lie Sp4 has dimension10. Strict equivalence uses the congruence kernel of GSp4, with fixed multiplier ε⁻¹. For nonempty T, define 𝒯 as the coordinate ring of (∏_{v∈T}GSp4-hat)/G_m-hat; it is Λ[[x₁,…,x_{11#T−1}]].
api: framed ring product after choosing a universal representative
unitTests: using Sp4 would give the wrong framing dimension

items.name: Framed global product
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real and ρ̄:G_{F⁺,S}→GSp4(k) absolutely irreducible of multiplier ε̄⁻¹. Let O be the coefficient DVR, Λ_v local coefficient rings and Λ their completed tensor product. Unlike §5, ad=Lie GSp4 has dimension11 and ad⁰=Lie Sp4 has dimension10. Strict equivalence uses the congruence kernel of GSp4, with fixed multiplier ε⁻¹. After choosing a universal representative, R_S^T≅R_S completed-tensor_Λ𝒯; the identification is choice-dependent but the formal relative dimension is intrinsic.

items.name: Regular symplectic Taylor–Wiles lifts
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real and ρ̄:G_{F⁺,S}→GSp4(k) absolutely irreducible of multiplier ε̄⁻¹. Let O be the coefficient DVR, Λ_v local coefficient rings and Λ their completed tensor product. Unlike §5, ad=Lie GSp4 has dimension11 and ad⁰=Lie Sp4 has dimension10. Strict equivalence uses the congruence kernel of GSp4, with fixed multiplier ε⁻¹. If q_v≡1 modp and residual Frobenius has four distinct ordered eigenvalues α₁,α₂,α₂⁻¹,α₁⁻¹, every lift is conjugate to a torus lift with characters γ₁,γ₂,γ₂⁻¹ε⁻¹,γ₁⁻¹ε⁻¹; the source root-coordinate argument must remove only off-torus conjugation.

items.name: Symplectic ordinary weight algebra
items.statement: Take F_v⁺=Q_p. Let Λ_GSp=O[[((Z_p×)^(p))²]], where (p) denotes the maximal pro-p quotient, and enlarge it by two universal unramified characters to Λ-tilde. Fix the ordered residual p-stabilization. A full symplectic flag means a complete flag with the required orthogonality relations. Λ_GSp parametrizes two ordered inertia characters; for p>2 it is a two-variable power-series algebra over O, while at2 its generic fibre has four components from the two C₂ factors.
unitTests: integral formal smoothness at2 cannot be inferred from generic regularity

items.name: Ordinary symplectic flag incidence scheme
items.statement: Take F_v⁺=Q_p. Let Λ_GSp=O[[((Z_p×)^(p))²]], where (p) denotes the maximal pro-p quotient, and enlarge it by two universal unramified characters to Λ-tilde. Fix the ordered residual p-stabilization. A full symplectic flag means a complete flag with the required orthogonality relations. Over the framed deformation ring and Λ-tilde, impose a stable full symplectic flag whose ordered graded characters are the two universal characters and their ε⁻¹-duals. The projection to the framed coefficient base is proper.
unitTests: a distinguished point has a unique flag
scalar unramified rank2 part admits multiple flags
a flag without symplectic orthogonality defines the GL4 problem
items.note: The named stage already states this object/interface. BCGP25 is an additional source/application; this classification does not claim implementation.

items.name: Ordinary GSp4 scheme-image ring
items.statement: Take F_v⁺=Q_p. Let Λ_GSp=O[[((Z_p×)^(p))²]], where (p) denotes the maximal pro-p quotient, and enlarge it by two universal unramified characters to Λ-tilde. Fix the ordered residual p-stabilization. A full symplectic flag means a complete flag with the required orthogonality relations. R_v△ is the scheme-theoretic image of that flag incidence projection. Do not remove p-torsion by definition; this differs from flat-closure ordinary rings elsewhere.
unitTests: a point with P1 of flags
p-flatness is a theorem when available, not part of this definition

items.name: Residual-distinguished flag uniqueness
items.statement: Take F_v⁺=Q_p. Let Λ_GSp=O[[((Z_p×)^(p))²]], where (p) denotes the maximal pro-p quotient, and enlarge it by two universal unramified characters to Λ-tilde. Fix the ordered residual p-stabilization. A full symplectic flag means a complete flag with the required orthogonality relations. If the ordered residual ordinary characters are distinct, the flag incidence projection is a closed immersion, giving the familiar residual-distinguished ordinary deformation ring.

items.name: Ordinary adjoint filtration
items.statement: Take F_v⁺=Q_p. Let Λ_GSp=O[[((Z_p×)^(p))²]], where (p) denotes the maximal pro-p quotient, and enlarge it by two universal unramified characters to Λ-tilde. Fix the ordered residual p-stabilization. A full symplectic flag means a complete flag with the required orthogonality relations. At a characteristic-zero flagged point, Fil^i ad⁰ consists of symplectic endomorphisms decreasing the flag by i; dimensions for i=0,…,4 are6,4,2,1,0.
unitTests: the trace orthogonal of Fil¹ has dimension6, not4

items.name: Ordinary obstruction duality
items.statement: Take F_v⁺=Q_p. Let Λ_GSp=O[[((Z_p×)^(p))²]], where (p) denotes the maximal pro-p quotient, and enlarge it by two universal unramified characters to Λ-tilde. Fix the ordered residual p-stabilization. A full symplectic flag means a complete flag with the required orthogonality relations. H²(G_Qp,Fil⁰ad⁰ρ_x)=0 exactly when H⁰(G_Qp,(ad⁰ρ_x/Fil¹)(1))=0, by the trace-dual filtration.

items.name: Flagged ordinary regularity
items.statement: Take F_v⁺=Q_p. Let Λ_GSp=O[[((Z_p×)^(p))²]], where (p) denotes the maximal pro-p quotient, and enlarge it by two universal unramified characters to Λ-tilde. Fix the ordered residual p-stabilization. A full symplectic flag means a complete flag with the required orthogonality relations. If this obstruction vanishes, x is a regular point of the characteristic-zero flag incidence scheme, on a unique component of dimension16.

items.name: Root-character obstruction criterion
items.statement: Take F_v⁺=Q_p. Let Λ_GSp=O[[((Z_p×)^(p))²]], where (p) denotes the maximal pro-p quotient, and enlarge it by two universal unramified characters to Λ-tilde. Fix the ordered residual p-stabilization. A full symplectic flag means a complete flag with the required orthogonality relations. The obstruction vanishes if none of χ̃₁²ε,χ̃₂²ε,χ̃₁χ̃₂ε,χ̃₁χ̃₂⁻¹ equals ε at x.

items.name: Pure distinguished obstruction criterion
items.statement: Take F_v⁺=Q_p. Let Λ_GSp=O[[((Z_p×)^(p))²]], where (p) denotes the maximal pro-p quotient, and enlarge it by two universal unramified characters to Λ-tilde. Fix the ordered residual p-stabilization. A full symplectic flag means a complete flag with the required orthogonality relations. The obstruction vanishes if ρ_x is pure and p-distinguished.

items.name: Pure potentially crystalline obstruction criterion
items.statement: Take F_v⁺=Q_p. Let Λ_GSp=O[[((Z_p×)^(p))²]], where (p) denotes the maximal pro-p quotient, and enlarge it by two universal unramified characters to Λ-tilde. Fix the ordered residual p-stabilization. A full symplectic flag means a complete flag with the required orthogonality relations. The obstruction also vanishes if ρ_x is pure and potentially crystalline; this statement concerns the flagged point.

items.name: Regularity on the ordinary ring
items.statement: Take F_v⁺=Q_p. Let Λ_GSp=O[[((Z_p×)^(p))²]], where (p) denotes the maximal pro-p quotient, and enlarge it by two universal unramified characters to Λ-tilde. Fix the ordered residual p-stabilization. A full symplectic flag means a complete flag with the required orthogonality relations. If ρ_x is p-distinguished and its flagged obstruction vanishes, the image point of Spec R_v△ is regular on a unique component of relative O-dimension16.

items.name: Common finite-flat ordinary weight-two component
items.statement: Take F_v⁺=Q_p. Let Λ_GSp=O[[((Z_p×)^(p))²]], where (p) denotes the maximal pro-p quotient, and enlarge it by two universal unramified characters to Λ-tilde. Fix the ordered residual p-stabilization. A full symplectic flag means a complete flag with the required orthogonality relations. For p>2 and finite-flat (ρ̄⊗ε̄), all ordinary pure weight2 crystalline lifts lie on one component of Spec R_v△, each on a unique component, of relative O-dimension16. The proof uses connected flag fibres and the rank4 symplectic adaptation of Kisin09 Lemma2.4.2/Proposition2.4.4.

items.name: Special-fibre point unique to a dominant component
items.statement: Take F_v⁺=Q_p. Let Λ_GSp=O[[((Z_p×)^(p))²]], where (p) denotes the maximal pro-p quotient, and enlarge it by two universal unramified characters to Λ-tilde. Fix the ordered residual p-stabilization. A full symplectic flag means a complete flag with the required orthogonality relations. For p>2, if a component R_v△/Q surjects onto Spec Λ_GSp, some special-fibre minimal prime contains Q and no other generic minimal prime; this component has relative O-dimension16. No assertion that every component dominates Λ is made.

items.name: Reasonable symplectic residual representation
items.statement: Let p>2, ρ̄:G_F→GSp4(k), and W=(sp4_k)∨ with the dual adjoint action. Definitions below are imported from Whitmore arXiv2205.05062v2 §§3.15–3.19, read on PDF pp21–23, and BCGP21 arXiv1812.09269v3 Definition7.5.11, PDF p201. For all sufficiently large n, H_n=ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{p^n})}) has H⁰(H_n,W)=0 and every nonzero simple k[H_n]-submodule W'⊂W is detected by some semisimple h∈H_n and z∈Lie Z(Z_GSp4(h))∩sp4, meaning w'(z)≠0 for some w'∈W'. Additionally, if ζ_p lies in the fixed field of W, require H¹(H_n,W)=0.
unitTests: detection may use a nonregular semisimple element
this is a representation condition, not merely an abstract-image name

items.name: Tidy residual image
items.statement: Let p>2, ρ̄:G_F→GSp4(k), and W=(sp4_k)∨ with the dual adjoint action. Definitions below are imported from Whitmore arXiv2205.05062v2 §§3.15–3.19, read on PDF pp21–23, and BCGP21 arXiv1812.09269v3 Definition7.5.11, PDF p201. A subgroup H⊂GSp4(k) is tidy if it contains h with ν(h)≠1 and no ratio of two eigenvalues of h equals ν(h); repeated eigenvalues are allowed. A representation is tidy when its image is.
unitTests: regular semisimplicity alone does not imply tidiness

items.name: Ordinary component through the automorphic seed
items.statement: Let p>2 split completely in totally real F⁺, and let π be an ordinary cuspidal GSp4 representation with central character absolute-value squared and weights (k_v,l_v;2). Its residual ρ̄ is GSp4-reasonable and tidy, ordinary of weight2 at p with stabilizations compatible with π; each π p-adic point lies on a unique component of R_v△. At the finite ramified set R away from p, ρ̄ is trivial, q_v≡1 modp (mod9 if p=3), and π has Iwahori fixed vectors. Choose the source neat auxiliary w₀ of residue characteristic>5, q_w₀ not≡1 modp and no residual eigenvalue ratio q_w₀. S_{1,π} uses the unique π component at each p-adic place, unipotent local types at R and the unrestricted smooth problem at w₀; its Hecke algebra is the corresponding ordinary localized quotient.
unitTests: a different local component is excluded
uniqueness is needed before selecting a component

items.name: Selected symplectic ordinary finiteness
items.statement: Let p>2 split completely in totally real F⁺, and let π be an ordinary cuspidal GSp4 representation with central character absolute-value squared and weights (k_v,l_v;2). Its residual ρ̄ is GSp4-reasonable and tidy, ordinary of weight2 at p with stabilizations compatible with π; each π p-adic point lies on a unique component of R_v△. At the finite ramified set R away from p, ρ̄ is trivial, q_v≡1 modp (mod9 if p=3), and π has Iwahori fixed vectors. Choose the source neat auxiliary w₀ of residue characteristic>5, q_w₀ not≡1 modp and no residual eigenvalue ratio q_w₀. R_{S_{1,π}} is finite over the symplectic ordinary weight algebra Λ_GSp,F⁺.

items.name: Selected symplectic ordinary reduced R=T
items.statement: Let p>2 split completely in totally real F⁺, and let π be an ordinary cuspidal GSp4 representation with central character absolute-value squared and weights (k_v,l_v;2). Its residual ρ̄ is GSp4-reasonable and tidy, ordinary of weight2 at p with stabilizations compatible with π; each π p-adic point lies on a unique component of R_v△. At the finite ramified set R away from p, ρ̄ is trivial, q_v≡1 modp (mod9 if p=3), and π has Iwahori fixed vectors. Choose the source neat auxiliary w₀ of residue characteristic>5, q_w₀ not≡1 modp and no residual eigenvalue ratio q_w₀. The map R_{S_{1,π}}→T_{S_{1,π}} has nilpotent kernel, giving reduced R=T on precisely the chosen local components.

items.name: Automorphic ordinary component dominates weight
items.statement: Let p>2 split completely in totally real F⁺, and let π be an ordinary cuspidal GSp4 representation with central character absolute-value squared and weights (k_v,l_v;2). Its residual ρ̄ is GSp4-reasonable and tidy, ordinary of weight2 at p with stabilizations compatible with π; each π p-adic point lies on a unique component of R_v△. At the finite ramified set R away from p, ρ̄ is trivial, q_v≡1 modp (mod9 if p=3), and π has Iwahori fixed vectors. Choose the source neat auxiliary w₀ of residue characteristic>5, q_w₀ not≡1 modp and no residual eigenvalue ratio q_w₀. The component through π dominates the local ordinary weight space by torsion-freeness and faithful action on the finite free ordinary module. This supplies the hypothesis of6.2.6 only where the proof needs it.

items.name: Regular semisimple classes at three
items.statement: Use the paper fixed embedding into GSp4(F3), multiplier ν and the subgroup labels in Table6.4.4. All claims about good reduction refer to an abelian surface with a polarization of degree prime to3. In GSp4(F3), the ν=1 regular classes have orders5,10,8; among ν=−1 there are five regular classes, two of order20 and three of order8, with the projective labels distinguished as in the table.

items.name: Finite-flat cyclotomic image stability
items.statement: If an abelian surface A/Q has good reduction at p>2, its mod-p image restricted to G_Q(ζ_p) equals its image on G_Q(ζ_{p^n}) for every n≥1. This is BCGP Lemma6.4.2, proved using the finite-flat ramification bound and the cyclotomic discriminant.

items.name: Fifteen allowed residual-three groups
items.statement: Use the paper fixed embedding into GSp4(F3), multiplier ν and the subgroup labels in Table6.4.4. All claims about good reduction refer to an abelian surface with a polarization of degree prime to3. For A/Q good at3, reasonable, tidy, and regular semisimple image both inside and outside Sp4(F3) hold exactly for the ticked Table6.4.4 groups:3.1620.1,3.1620.5,3.1620.10,3.1296.1,3.810.2,3.810.6,3.540.1,3.405.1,3.270.1,3.216.1,3.135.1,3.135.2,3.45.1,3.27.1,1.1.1. These labels require the pinned subgroup certificates, not name matching alone.

items.name: Failure of GL4 adequacy for the symplectic-three image
items.statement: Use the paper fixed embedding into GSp4(F3), multiplier ν and the subgroup labels in Table6.4.4. All claims about good reduction refer to an abelian surface with a polarization of degree prime to3. The natural Sp4(F3) representation has a nontrivial GL4 deformation direction in the exterior-square part, although the symplectic adjoint cohomology vanishes; consequently the p=3 argument cannot be replaced by the dyadic unitary adequacy theorem.

items.name: Integral enormity
items.statement: Let O be a p-adic coefficient DVR, E its fraction field, k its residue field, and H⊂GSp4(O) compact. The adjoint lattice ad⁰ is sp4_O; at p=2 it must not be identified with its O-dual through a supposedly unimodular trace pairing. H is integrally enormous when E⁴ is absolutely irreducible and, for each simple E[H]-submodule W⊂E⊗ad⁰, there is h∈H acting with eigenvalue1 on W whose reduction has four distinct eigenvalues on k⁴.
unitTests: Sp4 Zariski image with a residual regular element
rational regularity without residual regularity is insufficient

items.name: Sp4 image implies integral enormity
items.statement: Let O be a p-adic coefficient DVR, E its fraction field, k its residue field, and H⊂GSp4(O) compact. The adjoint lattice ad⁰ is sp4_O; at p=2 it must not be identified with its O-dual through a supposedly unimodular trace pairing. If the Zariski closure of H contains Sp4 and H has a residually regular semisimple element, then H is integrally enormous.

items.name: Induced image implies integral enormity
items.statement: Let O be a p-adic coefficient DVR, E its fraction field, k its residue field, and H⊂GSp4(O) compact. The adjoint lattice ad⁰ is sp4_O; at p=2 it must not be identified with its O-dual through a supposedly unimodular trace pairing. For H⊂Sp4(O) absolutely irreducible with an index-two subgroup whose Zariski closure contains SL2×SL2, a residually regular semisimple element outside that subgroup yields integral enormity, by the6+4 adjoint decomposition.

items.name: Cyclotomic integral enormity for full image
items.statement: For a continuous ρ:G_F⁺→GSp4(O) whose Zariski closure contains Sp4, if ρ̄(G_{F⁺(ζ_p)}) contains a regular semisimple element, then ρ(G_{F⁺(ζ_{p^∞})}) is integrally enormous. The pro-p tower argument supplies the required persistence; no separate assumed residual-image stability is needed.

items.name: Cyclotomic integral enormity for induced image
items.statement: Let F_∞ be the compositum of F⁺(ζ_{p^∞}) and the fixed field of the similitude character of ρ:G_F⁺→GSp4(O). If ρ is induced from a quadratic K/F⁺ disjoint from F_∞, its Zariski closure contains SL2×SL2, and ρ̄(G_F∞) outside ρ̄(G_KF∞) contains a regular semisimple element, then the cyclotomic-p-power image of ρ is integrally enormous.

items.name: Integral fixed-multiplier cohomology
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real with p completely split. Fix continuous ρ:G_F⁺→GSp4(O), unramified outside finite S⊃S_p, multiplier ε⁻¹, absolutely irreducible residual representation, pure, and ordinary semistable weight2 and p-distinguished at every p-adic place with fixed stabilizations. Require cyclotomic-p-power image integrally enormous; at2 require ρ̄(G_{F⁺(i)})=ρ̄(G_F⁺), and at odd p a residual regular element outside Sp4. Let R_S be the corresponding ordinary global ring, q its O-point kernel, and W=adρ, W⁰=ad⁰ρ. Define primed cohomology as the image of cohomology of W⁰ in that of W; retain separate finite quotients W_m, W⁰_m, E/O modules and characteristic-zero modules.
api: bounded discrepancy with W modulo its centre
unitTests: rational splitting does not imply integral splitting

items.name: Integral ordinary Selmer conditions
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real with p completely split. Fix continuous ρ:G_F⁺→GSp4(O), unramified outside finite S⊃S_p, multiplier ε⁻¹, absolutely irreducible residual representation, pure, and ordinary semistable weight2 and p-distinguished at every p-adic place with fixed stabilizations. Require cyclotomic-p-power image integrally enormous; at2 require ρ̄(G_{F⁺(i)})=ρ̄(G_F⁺), and at odd p a residual regular element outside Sp4. Let R_S be the corresponding ordinary global ring, q its O-point kernel, and W=adρ, W⁰=ad⁰ρ. Use the fixed local deformation tangent conditions and primed cohomology for the ordinary framed problem. The dual Selmer coefficients are (W⁰)* with Tate twist, with local conditions orthogonal to the chosen tangent spaces.
unitTests: dualizing W instead of W⁰ gives the wrong rank

items.name: Bounded lattice comparison error
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real with p completely split. Fix continuous ρ:G_F⁺→GSp4(O), unramified outside finite S⊃S_p, multiplier ε⁻¹, absolutely irreducible residual representation, pure, and ordinary semistable weight2 and p-distinguished at every p-adic place with fixed stabilizations. Require cyclotomic-p-power image integrally enormous; at2 require ρ̄(G_{F⁺(i)})=ρ̄(G_F⁺), and at odd p a residual regular element outside Sp4. Let R_S be the corresponding ordinary global ring, q its O-point kernel, and W=adρ, W⁰=ad⁰ρ. The isogeny between W⁰ and W modulo the scalar centre gives uniformly bounded differences of the relevant finite cohomology lengths as m varies.

items.name: Cotangent length through Selmer groups
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real with p completely split. Fix continuous ρ:G_F⁺→GSp4(O), unramified outside finite S⊃S_p, multiplier ε⁻¹, absolutely irreducible residual representation, pure, and ordinary semistable weight2 and p-distinguished at every p-adic place with fixed stabilizations. Require cyclotomic-p-power image integrally enormous; at2 require ρ̄(G_{F⁺(i)})=ρ̄(G_F⁺), and at odd p a residual regular element outside Sp4. Let R_S be the corresponding ordinary global ring, q its O-point kernel, and W=adρ, W⁰=ad⁰ρ. The length of the q-point relative cotangent module modulo π^m equals the primed Selmer length plus the sum of framed local H⁰(W_m) lengths minus global H⁰(W_m), with the fixed-multiplier deformation conventions.

items.name: Finite detection of rational dual Selmer
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real with p completely split. Fix continuous ρ:G_F⁺→GSp4(O), unramified outside finite S⊃S_p, multiplier ε⁻¹, absolutely irreducible residual representation, pure, and ordinary semistable weight2 and p-distinguished at every p-adic place with fixed stabilizations. Require cyclotomic-p-power image integrally enormous; at2 require ρ̄(G_{F⁺(i)})=ρ̄(G_F⁺), and at odd p a residual regular element outside Sp4. Let R_S be the corresponding ordinary global ring, q its O-point kernel, and W=adρ, W⁰=ad⁰ρ. If q is the O-corank of the E/O dual Selmer group, choose q residually regular cyclotomic elements whose joint restriction has finite kernel; integral enormity and purity detect every divisible direction.

items.name: Integral-enormity Taylor–Wiles datum
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real with p completely split. Fix continuous ρ:G_F⁺→GSp4(O), unramified outside finite S⊃S_p, multiplier ε⁻¹, absolutely irreducible residual representation, pure, and ordinary semistable weight2 and p-distinguished at every p-adic place with fixed stabilizations. Require cyclotomic-p-power image integrally enormous; at2 require ρ̄(G_{F⁺(i)})=ρ̄(G_F⁺), and at odd p a residual regular element outside Sp4. Let R_S be the corresponding ordinary global ring, q its O-point kernel, and W=adρ, W⁰=ad⁰ρ. A level-N set Q consists of primes outside S with q_v≡1 modp^N and four distinct residual Frobenius eigenvalues; retain their chosen ordering and impose unrestricted auxiliary local lifts.
api: two torus diamond coordinates per prime
unitTests: this differs from the repeated-eigenblock datum of §5

items.name: Uniform residual dual-Selmer bound
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real with p completely split. Fix continuous ρ:G_F⁺→GSp4(O), unramified outside finite S⊃S_p, multiplier ε⁻¹, absolutely irreducible residual representation, pure, and ordinary semistable weight2 and p-distinguished at every p-adic place with fixed stabilizations. Require cyclotomic-p-power image integrally enormous; at2 require ρ̄(G_{F⁺(i)})=ρ̄(G_F⁺), and at odd p a residual regular element outside Sp4. Let R_S be the corresponding ordinary global ring, q its O-point kernel, and W=adρ, W⁰=ad⁰ρ. There are Q_N of cardinality q with the remaining dual-Selmer length bounded independently of N, chosen by matching both finite Galois actions and cocycle values.

items.name: Linear cotangent bound
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real with p completely split. Fix continuous ρ:G_F⁺→GSp4(O), unramified outside finite S⊃S_p, multiplier ε⁻¹, absolutely irreducible residual representation, pure, and ordinary semistable weight2 and p-distinguished at every p-adic place with fixed stabilizations. Require cyclotomic-p-power image integrally enormous; at2 require ρ̄(G_{F⁺(i)})=ρ̄(G_F⁺), and at odd p a residual regular element outside Sp4. Let R_S be the corresponding ordinary global ring, q its O-point kernel, and W=adρ, W⁰=ad⁰ρ. For these Q_N and m≤N the relative cotangent length is at most d₂+m(2q−4[F⁺:Q]+#S−1), for one uniform d₂.

items.name: Almost presentation at the characteristic-zero point
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real with p completely split. Fix continuous ρ:G_F⁺→GSp4(O), unramified outside finite S⊃S_p, multiplier ε⁻¹, absolutely irreducible residual representation, pure, and ordinary semistable weight2 and p-distinguished at every p-adic place with fixed stabilizations. Require cyclotomic-p-power image integrally enormous; at2 require ρ̄(G_{F⁺(i)})=ρ̄(G_F⁺), and at odd p a residual regular element outside Sp4. Let R_S be the corresponding ordinary global ring, q its O-point kernel, and W=adρ, W⁰=ad⁰ρ. Put g=2q−4[F⁺:Q]+#S−1. For every N there is R_loc[[X₁,…,X_g]]→R^S_{S_QN} whose relative q-cotangent cokernel is killed by one π^d independent of N. The map is not asserted surjective.

items.name: Characteristic-zero patching data
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real with p completely split. Fix continuous ρ:G_F⁺→GSp4(O), unramified outside finite S⊃S_p, multiplier ε⁻¹, absolutely irreducible residual representation, pure, and ordinary semistable weight2 and p-distinguished at every p-adic place with fixed stabilizations. Require cyclotomic-p-power image integrally enormous; at2 require ρ̄(G_{F⁺(i)})=ρ̄(G_F⁺), and at odd p a residual regular element outside Sp4. Let R_S be the corresponding ordinary global ring, q its O-point kernel, and W=adρ, W⁰=ad⁰ρ. Take an R_S-module M finite free over Λ, quotients Δ_N of Δ_∞=Z_p^{2q} mapping onto Δ_∞/p^N, finite modules M_N free over Λ[Δ_N] and equivariant augmentation isomorphisms (M_N)_{Δ_N}≅M.
unitTests: module isomorphism without compatible ring action is insufficient

items.name: Corrected finite-open-quotient patched module
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real with p completely split. Fix continuous ρ:G_F⁺→GSp4(O), unramified outside finite S⊃S_p, multiplier ε⁻¹, absolutely irreducible residual representation, pure, and ordinary semistable weight2 and p-distinguished at every p-adic place with fixed stabilizations. Require cyclotomic-p-power image integrally enormous; at2 require ρ̄(G_{F⁺(i)})=ρ̄(G_F⁺), and at odd p a residual regular element outside Sp4. Let R_S be the corresponding ordinary global ring, q its O-point kernel, and W=adρ, W⁰=ad⁰ρ. With S_∞=Λ[[Δ_∞]] completed-tensor𝒯, patch framed M_N using finite open/maximal-ideal or mixed(π^n,a_∞^n) quotients, and take the compatible inverse limit. The printed augmentation-only quotients are not eventually compatible: (1+T)^{p^N}−1 is never in(T²) over O.

items.name: Compatible patched ring action
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real with p completely split. Fix continuous ρ:G_F⁺→GSp4(O), unramified outside finite S⊃S_p, multiplier ε⁻¹, absolutely irreducible residual representation, pure, and ordinary semistable weight2 and p-distinguished at every p-adic place with fixed stabilizations. Require cyclotomic-p-power image integrally enormous; at2 require ρ̄(G_{F⁺(i)})=ρ̄(G_F⁺), and at odd p a residual regular element outside Sp4. Let R_S be the corresponding ordinary global ring, q its O-point kernel, and W=adρ, W⁰=ad⁰ρ. Patch R_N using matching open ideals and joint ring/module truncations; construct S_∞→R_patch, R_∞→R_patch and the action on M_∞, its finite freeness over S_∞ and its augmentation to M. The dyadic lift S_∞→R_∞ requires a separate argument after characteristic-zero component completion; integral formal smoothness of Λ is unavailable.

items.name: Uniform patched cotangent annihilator
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real with p completely split. Fix continuous ρ:G_F⁺→GSp4(O), unramified outside finite S⊃S_p, multiplier ε⁻¹, absolutely irreducible residual representation, pure, and ordinary semistable weight2 and p-distinguished at every p-adic place with fixed stabilizations. Require cyclotomic-p-power image integrally enormous; at2 require ρ̄(G_{F⁺(i)})=ρ̄(G_F⁺), and at odd p a residual regular element outside Sp4. Let R_S be the corresponding ordinary global ring, q its O-point kernel, and W=adρ, W⁰=ad⁰ρ. The finite-level π^d bound passes to q_patch/(q_patch²,q_∞R_patch) for a compatible open-ideal patched system.

items.name: Characteristic-zero patched freeness
items.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real with p completely split. Fix continuous ρ:G_F⁺→GSp4(O), unramified outside finite S⊃S_p, multiplier ε⁻¹, absolutely irreducible residual representation, pure, and ordinary semistable weight2 and p-distinguished at every p-adic place with fixed stabilizations. Require cyclotomic-p-power image integrally enormous; at2 require ρ̄(G_{F⁺(i)})=ρ̄(G_F⁺), and at odd p a residual regular element outside Sp4. Let R_S be the corresponding ordinary global ring, q its O-point kernel, and W=adρ, W⁰=ad⁰ρ. For a patching system satisfying7.2.1 and the corrected ring-action construction, M_q is finite free over (R_S)_q: pure distinguished local regularity, cotangent surjectivity after inverting p, depth and Auslander–Buchsbaum give the result. Rank zero is possible until nonvanishing is proved.

items.name: Four higher-Hida modules
items.statement: Now F⁺=Q. For each w∈{}^MW use the perfect ordinary higher-Hida cusp complex in amplitudes[0,ℓ(w)] or noncusp complex in[ℓ(w),3]. Define M_w to be degreeℓ(w) of the cusp complex when ℓ(w)=0,1 and of the noncusp complex when ℓ(w)=2,3, over O[[T(Z_p)]]. M_w is the source choice of extremal cohomology of the ordinary perfect complex, with its tame Hecke action, weight algebra and level functoriality; retain the cusp/noncusp choice in each length.
api: pullback and trace in tame level
unitTests: using cusp top cohomology for all four w changes the theorem

items.name: Projectivity of higher-Hida modules
items.statement: Now F⁺=Q. For each w∈{}^MW use the perfect ordinary higher-Hida cusp complex in amplitudes[0,ℓ(w)] or noncusp complex in[ℓ(w),3]. Define M_w to be degreeℓ(w) of the cusp complex when ℓ(w)=0,1 and of the noncusp complex when ℓ(w)=2,3, over O[[T(Z_p)]]. Each M_w is finite projective over O[[T(Z_p)]].

items.name: Classical higher-Hida control
items.statement: Now F⁺=Q. For each w∈{}^MW use the perfect ordinary higher-Hida cusp complex in amplitudes[0,ℓ(w)] or noncusp complex in[ℓ(w),3]. Define M_w to be degreeℓ(w) of the cusp complex when ℓ(w)=0,1 and of the noncusp complex when ℓ(w)=2,3, over O[[T(Z_p)]]. For dominant algebraic λ and κ=−w₀,M w(λ+ρ)−ρ, specializing M_w via λ and tensoring E(−λ) gives ordinary coherent H^{ℓ(w)} at Iwahori p-level, with boundary ideal exactly when ℓ(w)=0,1.

items.name: Higher-Coleman control
items.statement: Now F⁺=Q. For each w∈{}^MW use the perfect ordinary higher-Hida cusp complex in amplitudes[0,ℓ(w)] or noncusp complex in[ℓ(w),3]. Define M_w to be degreeℓ(w) of the cusp complex when ℓ(w)=0,1 and of the noncusp complex when ℓ(w)=2,3, over O[[T(Z_p)]]. For algebraic λ such that the same κ is M-dominant, specialization gives ordinary T(Z_p)-invariant supported coherent H^{ℓ(w)}_w at infinite p-level, with the same boundary convention.

items.name: Perfect higher-Hida duality
items.statement: Now F⁺=Q. For each w∈{}^MW use the perfect ordinary higher-Hida cusp complex in amplitudes[0,ℓ(w)] or noncusp complex in[ℓ(w),3]. Define M_w to be degreeℓ(w) of the cusp complex when ℓ(w)=0,1 and of the noncusp complex when ℓ(w)=2,3, over O[[T(Z_p)]]. There is a perfect weight-algebra pairing M_w⊗M_{w₀,Mww₀}→O[[T(Z_p)]] interpolating classical Serre duality.

items.name: Tame group-algebra projectivity
items.statement: Now F⁺=Q. For each w∈{}^MW use the perfect ordinary higher-Hida cusp complex in amplitudes[0,ℓ(w)] or noncusp complex in[ℓ(w),3]. Define M_w to be degreeℓ(w) of the cusp complex when ℓ(w)=0,1 and of the noncusp complex when ℓ(w)=2,3, over O[[T(Z_p)]]. For normal K₁^p⊂K₂^p, M_{w,K₁^p} is finite projective over O[[T(Z_p)]][K₂^p/K₁^p].

items.name: Tame invariant and coinvariant control
items.statement: Now F⁺=Q. For each w∈{}^MW use the perfect ordinary higher-Hida cusp complex in amplitudes[0,ℓ(w)] or noncusp complex in[ℓ(w),3]. Define M_w to be degreeℓ(w) of the cusp complex when ℓ(w)=0,1 and of the noncusp complex when ℓ(w)=2,3, over O[[T(Z_p)]]. Pullback identifies M at K₂^p with invariants at K₁^p, and trace identifies coinvariants at K₁^p with M at K₂^p.

items.name: Projectivity test by derived coinvariants
items.statement: Now F⁺=Q. For each w∈{}^MW use the perfect ordinary higher-Hida cusp complex in amplitudes[0,ℓ(w)] or noncusp complex in[ℓ(w),3]. Define M_w to be degreeℓ(w) of the cusp complex when ℓ(w)=0,1 and of the noncusp complex when ℓ(w)=2,3, over O[[T(Z_p)]]. For finite group G, CNL coefficient ring R and finite R[G]-module M, projectivity is equivalent to freeness on a p-Sylow H, and to the source derived H-coinvariant complex being free over R in degree0; reduction to the residue field gives the equivalent derived test.

items.name: Split-torus character dictionary
items.statement: Now F⁺=Q. For each w∈{}^MW use the perfect ordinary higher-Hida cusp complex in amplitudes[0,ℓ(w)] or noncusp complex in[ℓ(w),3]. Define M_w to be degreeℓ(w) of the cusp complex when ℓ(w)=0,1 and of the noncusp complex when ℓ(w)=2,3, over O[[T(Z_p)]]. For split T and coefficient rings in the source setting, Hom(T(R),S×) identifies with Hom(R×,T-dual(S)) through the character/cocharacter lattices, naturally in both rings.

items.name: Hida-to-Galois weight map
items.statement: Now F⁺=Q. For each w∈{}^MW use the perfect ordinary higher-Hida cusp complex in amplitudes[0,ℓ(w)] or noncusp complex in[ℓ(w),3]. Define M_w to be degreeℓ(w) of the cusp complex when ℓ(w)=0,1 and of the noncusp complex when ℓ(w)=2,3, over O[[T(Z_p)]]. There is a unique map from the automorphic torus weight algebra to Λ_GSp,Q carrying the normalized universal character χ_unρν^{−3/2} to ψ(z)=diag(χ₁(z),χ₂(z),z⁻¹χ₂(z)⁻¹,z⁻¹χ₁(z)⁻¹).

items.name: Central-character higher-Hida summand
items.statement: Now F⁺=Q. For each w∈{}^MW use the perfect ordinary higher-Hida cusp complex in amplitudes[0,ℓ(w)] or noncusp complex in[ℓ(w),3]. Define M_w to be degreeℓ(w) of the cusp complex when ℓ(w)=0,1 and of the noncusp complex when ℓ(w)=2,3, over O[[T(Z_p)]]. After the weight base change, impose central character absolute-value squared, partially outside a finite S or fully; at p this is the z_p⁻² action on the centre.
unitTests: a scalar centre action cannot be inferred from trace alone

items.name: Partial-centre projectivity
items.statement: Now F⁺=Q. For each w∈{}^MW use the perfect ordinary higher-Hida cusp complex in amplitudes[0,ℓ(w)] or noncusp complex in[ℓ(w),3]. Define M_w to be degreeℓ(w) of the cusp complex when ℓ(w)=0,1 and of the noncusp complex when ℓ(w)=2,3, over O[[T(Z_p)]]. For a prime r>5 with r not≡1 modp if p>2, or r not≡1 mod4 if p=2, fix Iw₁(r) at both normal tame levels. If r∈S and p∉S, the partial-central-character module at K₁^p is finite projective over Λ[Z^S K₂^p/Z^S K₁^p].

items.name: Full-centre projectivity
