Preserve its Drinfeld/Lubin–Tate and p-adic local Langlands endpoints. Its Dospinescu–Le Bras extension already explicitly owns Stein spaces in every dimension, Kiehl acyclicity and Chiarellotto/Grosse-Klönne duality. Add the coherent compact-support interface used by BCGP25 §4.6: define cohomology with proper closed supports and its relatively compact exhaustion comparison; for smooth Stein X of pure dimension d and finite locally free F, prove concentration of H_c(X,F) in degree d and the perfect continuous pairing with H⁰(Hom(F,Ω^d)). Prove compact-type LB structure and naturality under coefficient maps. Import adic coherent sheaves and Čech comparison from AdicSpacesPartII:R3, and Banach–Smith exact duality from LocallyAnalyticDistributionsPartIIQuasiAbelianFunctionalAnalysis. The latter owns infinite-dimensional tensor refinements, avoiding a duplicate functional-analysis construction here. The geometric Stein layers must precede and be independent of both the Drinfeld tower applications and higher Coleman theory: neither consumer is an input to the general duality. Retain smoothness and pure dimension, which are essential in BCGP Corollary4.6.26. Suggested future file: TauCeti/Geometry/Adic/Stein/CoherentDuality.lean, beside the already proposed tower files.
routes.reason: The pending tower proposal already includes the generic all-dimensional Stein duality foundation; reuse that identity and expose the reusable layers to higher Coleman theory.
The generic completed cohomology/homology tower and its Hecke/duality interface have this owner; no GL2 geometric comparison is treated as a GSp4 theorem.
Import Igusa towers and source-qualified boundary/concentration theorems; decomposed genericity and irreducible localization are distinct conditions.
Own continuous Galois representations, inertia/Frobenius conventions and the foundational cohomology/compatibility interface used in the arithmetic applications.
Own polarized global deformation functors, their tangent/dual-Selmer conditions and auxiliary-prime constructions; near adequacy and integral enormity must retain their distinct hypotheses.

routes.title: Ordinary automorphic forms and modularity lifting, Part II: dyadic unitary and symplectic ordinary lifting
routes.brief: The parent R21 roadmap is modular/Hilbert/quaternionic rank2 ordinary theory, particularly Skinner–Wiles. Add the genuinely new higher-rank cases of BCGP25 §§5–6 without broadening a rank2 layer by name alone. The first endpoint is Theorem5.7.14: for the specified everywhere-unramified CM extension with2 split, ordinary RACSDC residual automorphy, absolute irreducibility, near adequacy, a regular semisimple residual element, the parity condition n[F⁺:Q]≡0 mod4 and strong residual oddness when n is even, the sufficiently-deep ordinary deformation ring is finite over the weight algebra and its reduction equals the ordinary Hecke algebra. Preserve all splitting/ramification/local deformation hypotheses and the G_n-conjugacy relation; at2 the GL1 component changes tangent conditions. Taylor–Wiles kills all but the unavoidable one-dimensional dual-Selmer class. The second endpoint is Theorem6.3.4 for p>2 completely split in F⁺: the specified reasonable/tidy ordinary residual GSp4 system on the chosen local components through π has finite weight algebra and reduced R=T. Import local GSp4 scheme-image/ordinary-component geometry from LocalGaloisDeformationRings, global deformation and auxiliary-prime cohomology from GlobalGaloisDeformations, generic patching/support from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra, Hida families from PadicFamilies/HigherHidaAndColemanTheory, and ACC+ ordinary CM/support/base-change infrastructure from PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure. Import unitary automorphic spaces and transfer from AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups and EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison. The p=3 residual symplectic image need not be adequate as a GL4 image, so the two lifting branches cannot be merged into one unsupported adequacy hypothesis. Include source-verified tests for the one surviving dyadic Selmer class, the four dyadic weight components after inverting2, and the distinction between an arbitrary local component and the chosen automorphic component. This project proves regular-weight lifting; singular classicality and the2–3 switch are downstream.
routes.reason: The higher-rank/dyadic theorems go beyond the existing rank2 parent. Generic deformation and patching constructions stay with their current owners.
Import the existing Cartier-duality carrier and plan only the missing ordinary BT, finite-flat cohomology and polarized deformation comparisons here.
Own convolution, Jacquet modules and Satake. The GSp4 Iwahori calculation is a source within these layers, with its full central character.
Semistable reduction, torus lattices and specialization are imported into the explicit2–3 switch, not reconstructed there.

routes.title: Locally analytic representations of p-adic reductive groups
routes.brief: Join the existing proposal of PAPER-DING-25, also used by PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-20. Add BCGP25's solid locally profinite and analytic representation categories, smooth and λ-smooth objects, analytic-vector construction with its three actions, Banach analytic-group/distribution equivalence, and enough-injectives results. Import D(G) and coadmissible module foundations from the pending NoncommutativeAnalyticDistributions rather than duplicating their construction; import Banach–Smith duality from the pending functional-analysis Part II. The group's analytic action, continuity, Banach-stage integrability, and algebraic coaction are distinct predicates. Construct the derived locally analytic-vector interface in the exact source generality. For dependency order, the category-O algebraic core is supplied by LieHighestWeightPartIICompletedCategoryO, since upstream LieHighestWeight explicitly excludes full category O. The Orlik–Strauch layers of the existing Ding brief consume that core; the new HCS localization construction does not import the Orlik–Strauch output. Only the foundational representation stages are used by the analytic category-O stages, so the stage graph must make this order explicit and contain no return edge through the later Orlik–Strauch theorem. Preserve the Ding and CDN terminal theorems unchanged and add these foundational interfaces once.
routes.reason: The atlas already has a pending locally analytic representation roadmap; this paper extends that same identity and resolves its foundational ownership overlap.

routes.title: Modularity and Langlands extensions, Part II: GSp4 local Langlands and Galois representations
routes.brief: Coalesce with the same pending roadmap proposed by PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21; do not create another GSp4 interface. This addition owns the specialist adapters in BCGP25 Theorem1.8.13 and Proposition7.5.1. For regular algebraic cuspidal GSp4 over a totally real field with p completely split and central character absolute-value squared, construct the semisimple symplectic Galois representation of multiplier ε⁻¹, its geometric-Frobenius local-global comparison, Hodge–Tate weights and ordinary diagonal exactly as split in1.8.13. Under irreducibility obtain purity and full Frobenius-semisimplified Weil–Deligne compatibility. For a general-type local packet identify its unique generic paramodular member, prove its minimal paramodular invariant line is one-dimensional, and identify the minimum level with the local parameter conductor. Import the generic regular GL_n Galois construction from AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII, transfer and multiplicity from EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison, smooth convolution/Jacquet/Satake from SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, and the common integral Hecke reconstruction from IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants. Do not reconstruct those generic foundations in this Part II. Preserve the companion's Gan–Takeda correspondence and GSp4-specific packet scope; a GL4 representation alone does not encode a chosen similitude. Singular weight2 interpolation remains a consumer in GSp4NonregularModularityLifting, not an input to this regular package. The newform proof must read Roberts–Schmidt, Schmidt and Johnson-Leung–Roberts–Schmidt in their stated local ranges. Suggested future files: TauCeti/Automorphic/GSp4/{LocalLanglands,RegularGalois,ParamodularNewforms}.lean. Retain the Arthur dependency registry; this extraction does not claim the pending proposal is already a designed or implemented roadmap.
routes.reason: The newly merged BCGP21 extraction proposes this specialist interface. These seven items refine it; general automorphic, Hecke and deformation inputs retain their existing owners.

contexts.conventions: E is a sufficiently large finite extension of Q_p, O its integers and k its residue field. Galois representations are continuous. Hodge–Tate(ε)=−1 and Sen(ε)=1; local reciprocity sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius. Statements using Arthur classification retain the twisted weighted fundamental lemma dependency of §1.6.
contexts.main-A: Use H1, geometric Frobenius and the GSp4 normalization in §1.8. Retain the Arthur input and the source-proof obligations recorded in sourceIssues.
contexts.baseline: Library statements below were read at Mathlib082e2d3 and TauCeti f790474; their limited scope is part of the assertion.
contexts.solid-analysis: Fix a sufficiently large universe and a finite extension E/Q_p. Work in solid modules for the analytic ring E with E_solid[S]=E⊗Z_solid[S], not the naive general-R IsSolid predicate at the pinned baseline. Tensor products and duals in this section are solid/internal unless stated otherwise.
contexts.enveloping: Let g be the Lie algebra of a split reductive E-group, with chosen integral model and shrinking analytic identity neighborhoods. Use the upstream field PBW theorem as an import; the pinned general PBW result is only spanning.
contexts.lie-homology: Let G/E be split reductive, B,T fixed, P=MU_P standard, w a Weyl representative, p_w and m_w the conjugate parabolic and Levi, and d=dim u_p. Lie homology is E⊗^L_{U(u)}M in nonpositive cohomological degrees; cohomology is RHom_{U(u)}(E,M).
contexts.twisted-verma: Keep the split reductive G,E,B,T data. In §2.4 the field E is used discretely when forming Z-solid analytic stacks. Put FL=B\G and d_FL=dim FL; w ranges over the Weyl group.
contexts.topology: Use finite-dimensional weight spaces with chosen bases for O-modules, and PBW multiindices (not adjoint weight spaces) for U(g). Let abs(ν)=1+Σabs(n_i) in a fixed weight-lattice basis.
contexts.analytic-sheaves: Let C/E be a complete rank-one valued extension, X an adic space locally of finite type over C, G a split reductive analytic group, P a parabolic, and FL=P\G. Work with solid E-sheaves and solid O_X-modules; retain the local Banach-stage and analytic-integrability conditions in every equivariant category.
contexts.bruhat-sheaves: Continue with FL=P\G and a parabolic Q⊃B. C_{w,Q}=P\PwQ is a Q-orbit, C_{w,Q}† its dagger germ in FL, and P_w=w⁻¹Pw. All LB categories retain the stated compatible Banach-stage analytic actions.
contexts.HCS: Let O(g,q) be the parabolic category O for Q⊃B: the relevant Levi acts locally finitely and the Cartan semisimply. Let λ be a Lie character of Q and O(g,q)_{λ-alg} the subcategory whose weights differ from λ by algebraic characters.
contexts.localization: Keep the split reductive analytic G, parabolic P, d=dim U_P and Cla from §3.2. Let M be a finitely generated U(g)-module, with B-character twists used only when specified; Loc is a contravariant derived functor.
contexts.singular-localization: Specialize G=GSp4, P the Siegel parabolic, Q the Klingen parabolic for β, and write w₃=w₀^M, w₂=w₃s_β. Let λ=(1,1;w) with even w, η=(0,−1;1), and μ₀=−1−w/2. The Q-orbit is a P1-fibration with closed w₂ cell and open w₃ cell.
contexts.hodge-type-tower: Fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), a neat tame level K^p, p-adic coefficient field E large enough for the split group and reflex embeddings, and compatible toroidal cone decompositions. Write Sh^tor_{K^p} for the infinite-p-level tower over C_p, FL=P\G for its Hodge–Tate flag variety, μ for the Hodge cocharacter, d=dim Sh and D for the boundary. The G(Q_p)-action changes cone data when necessary; comparisons are taken after compatible refinement.
contexts.higher-coefficients: Keep the Hodge-type tower and d from §4.2. For w∈{}^MW let P_w=w⁻¹Pw, m_w its Levi Lie algebra, λ a character of the relevant Borel, and M∈O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. HCS_{w,λ} is the exact contravariant sheaf functor of §3.4. Coefficients on the tower are VB^0(HCS_{w,λ}(M)).
contexts.analytic-cohomology: Let E be a complete nonarchimedean coefficient field of characteristic zero. Use rigid/adic analytic spaces over E with the specified affinoid, quasi-Stein or smooth Stein hypotheses; all tensor products and duals in the coefficient refinements are solid/continuous as specified.
contexts.formal-coefficients: Let 𝔛 be the admissible formal O_E-model in §4.6.36, with generic fibre X; p-adic completeness refers to the displayed sheaf inverse limit, not merely completeness of individual stalks.
contexts.Coleman-amplitudes: Use the Hodge-type tower, HCS and HC_{w,λ} defined above, with d=dim Sh and w∈{}^MW. Coefficients M belong to O(m_w,b_{m_w})_{λ-alg}. The integral models are obtained on modified toroidal formal models from the small Levi torsor.
contexts.ES: Use the Hodge-type tower. Let λ be a Lie character of B and M∈O(g,b)_{λ-alg}. Define CC_λ(M) from locally analytic completed cohomology by derived g-Hom from M with its integrated −λ B-twist; cusp denotes the compact-support completed complex. Sen weights follow the paper convention ε has Sen weight+1.
contexts.Siegel-ES: Specialize to GSp4 and d=3, with the paper Borel and four representatives w_j of length j. For algebraic G-dominant κ=(k₁,k₂;w), 0≥k₁≥k₂ and the parity condition holds; write V_κ for its algebraic representation. Classical coherent bundles here have the untwisted normalization of §4.8.
contexts.Siegel-ordinary: Let λ=(λ₁,λ₂;w) be non-Liouville, with GSp4 conventions as above. Take ordinary parts of the Verma/Borel derived completed complex. H^i_{w_j} denotes ordinary cohomology of the corresponding big coefficient of weight −w₀,M(w_j·λ+2ρ^M), with the B-character twist −w_j⁻¹w₀,Mρ−ρ. A residual localization is at a continuous irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p-bar), with maximal ideal specified by the P_ℓ geometric-Frobenius polynomial.
contexts.singular-Sen: Set λ=(1,1;w) for even w and retain the irreducible residual localization. Let V be degree3 ordinary Borel completed cohomology, with the four Bruhat pieces and their character twists. Set a=−1−w/2 and b=−2−w/2.
contexts.Galois-semisimplicity: Let E/Q_p be finite and enlarge coefficients as needed. Continuous G_Q-representations are unramified outside finitely many primes. Polynomial-annihilation conditions below are required on a density-one set of unramified Frobenius classes, not merely equality of traces.
contexts.weight-two-classicality: Let f be an ordinary overconvergent GSp4 eigenform of coherent weight (2,2;−w), w even, with smooth torus eigencharacter χ_f and maximal ideal m_f. Its Hecke polynomial is P_ℓ, for geometric Frobenius, so the interpolated representation is normalized as ρ_π∨ε⁻³. Let λ=(1,1;w), and V=H³ of the ordinary Borel completed complex localized at m_{ρ̄_f}.
contexts.unitary-polarization: Let F/F⁺ be CM with F⁺ totally real, c a chosen complex conjugation and O the integers of a sufficiently large finite extension E/Q₂ with residue field k. For a coefficient ring R, G_n=(GL_n×GL₁)⋊{1,j}, where j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a); its multiplier is ν(g,a)=a and ν(j)=−1.
contexts.near-adequacy: Let V=k^n for a subfield k⊂F₂-bar and finite H⊂GL(V), with ad=End_k(V) carrying conjugation and ad⁰=ker(trace). All group-cohomology coefficients and trace projectors below use this characteristic2 representation.
contexts.dyadic-deformation: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, places above2 split, S includes the archimedean and2-adic places and all ramification, and r̄:G_{F⁺,S}→G_n(k) has absolutely irreducible restriction ρ̄ to G_F. Fix an odd lift χ of the multiplier. For each v∈S choose a CNL_O coefficient algebra Λ_v and a conjugation-stable fixed-multiplier local deformation condition; Λ is their completed tensor product. The global domain is G_F⁺, not G_F.
contexts.dyadic-local-rings: Use the dyadic polarized deformation setup and a finite place v split in F. At places away from2 the residue cardinality is q_v; at v above2 use the ordered universal inertia characters on the pro2 torus weight algebra Λ_{GL_n,v}.
contexts.definite-unitary-ordinary: Assume F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, every2-adic place split, n≥2 and n[F⁺:Q] divisible by4. Let G be the definite unitary group compact at infinity and quasi-split at finite places, identified with GL_n at split places. Fix the source tame level U, ordinary p-levels and a non-Eisenstein residual automorphic maximal ideal m.
contexts.symplectic-deformation: Let F⁺ be totally real and ρ̄:G_{F⁺,S}→GSp4(k) absolutely irreducible of multiplier ε̄⁻¹. Let O be the coefficient DVR, Λ_v local coefficient rings and Λ their completed tensor product. Unlike §5, ad=Lie GSp4 has dimension11 and ad⁰=Lie Sp4 has dimension10. Strict equivalence uses the congruence kernel of GSp4, with fixed multiplier ε⁻¹.
contexts.ordinary-GSp-local: Take F_v⁺=Q_p. Let Λ_GSp=O[[((Z_p×)^(p))²]], where (p) denotes the maximal pro-p quotient, and enlarge it by two universal unramified characters to Λ-tilde. Fix the ordered residual p-stabilization. A full symplectic flag means a complete flag with the required orthogonality relations.
contexts.image-predicates: Let p>2, ρ̄:G_F→GSp4(k), and W=(sp4_k)∨ with the dual adjoint action. Definitions below are imported from Whitmore arXiv2205.05062v2 §§3.15–3.19, read on PDF pp21–23, and BCGP21 arXiv1812.09269v3 Definition7.5.11, PDF p201.
contexts.odd-prime-lifting: Let p>2 split completely in totally real F⁺, and let π be an ordinary cuspidal GSp4 representation with central character absolute-value squared and weights (k_v,l_v;2). Its residual ρ̄ is GSp4-reasonable and tidy, ordinary of weight2 at p with stabilizations compatible with π; each π p-adic point lies on a unique component of R_v△. At the finite ramified set R away from p, ρ̄ is trivial, q_v≡1 modp (mod9 if p=3), and π has Iwahori fixed vectors. Choose the source neat auxiliary w₀ of residue characteristic>5, q_w₀ not≡1 modp and no residual eigenvalue ratio q_w₀.
contexts.residual-three: Use the paper fixed embedding into GSp4(F3), multiplier ν and the subgroup labels in Table6.4.4. All claims about good reduction refer to an abelian surface with a polarization of degree prime to3.
contexts.integral-enormity: Let O be a p-adic coefficient DVR, E its fraction field, k its residue field, and H⊂GSp4(O) compact. The adjoint lattice ad⁰ is sp4_O; at p=2 it must not be identified with its O-dual through a supposedly unimodular trace pairing.
contexts.integral-TW: Let F⁺ be totally real with p completely split. Fix continuous ρ:G_F⁺→GSp4(O), unramified outside finite S⊃S_p, multiplier ε⁻¹, absolutely irreducible residual representation, pure, and ordinary semistable weight2 and p-distinguished at every p-adic place with fixed stabilizations. Require cyclotomic-p-power image integrally enormous; at2 require ρ̄(G_{F⁺(i)})=ρ̄(G_F⁺), and at odd p a residual regular element outside Sp4. Let R_S be the corresponding ordinary global ring, q its O-point kernel, and W=adρ, W⁰=ad⁰ρ.
contexts.higher-Hida: Now F⁺=Q. For each w∈{}^MW use the perfect ordinary higher-Hida cusp complex in amplitudes[0,ℓ(w)] or noncusp complex in[ℓ(w),3]. Define M_w to be degreeℓ(w) of the cusp complex when ℓ(w)=0,1 and of the noncusp complex when ℓ(w)=2,3, over O[[T(Z_p)]].
contexts.auxiliary-Hecke: Retain Hypothesis7.1.3 over Q and the four higher-Hida modules. The arithmetic Hecke polynomial here is Q_ℓ for ρ, not the geometric dual-spin P_ℓ used in §4. Fix the full central character and ordered residual p-stabilization; write Λ=Λ_GSp,Q.
contexts.paramodular-multiplicity: Use a pure ordinary semistable weight2 distinguished ρ:G_Q→GSp4(O) of multiplier ε⁻¹, absolutely irreducible residual representation and cyclotomic integral enormity as in7.1.3. Choose the neat prime r and away-from-p,r paramodular level at the conductor of ρ; let q be its point of R_S and M one of the four localized higher-Hida multiplicity modules.
contexts.nonregular-lifting-endpoint: Let ρ:G_Q→GSp4(O) be continuous, unramified at all but finitely many primes, of multiplier ε⁻¹, pure, ordinary semistable weight2 and p-distinguished at p, with cyclotomic-p-power image integrally enormous. Require one of the following seed packages. (A) p=2: a solvable CM F/Q and ordinary RACSDC GL4/F form π with residual representation ρ̄ restricted to G_F, nearly adequate image containing a regular semisimple element, strongly residually odd polarized pair(ρ̄ restricted to G_F,1) at some real place, and ρ̄(G_Q(i))=ρ̄(G_Q). (B) p>2: an ordinary cuspidal GSp4/Q form π of central character absolute-value squared with residual representation ρ̄, which is reasonable and tidy, a regular residual element outside Sp4, and compatible p-stabilizations such that ρ_π lies on a unique ordinary local component and ρ lies on that same component. Use paramodular conductor level and a neat auxiliary prime as above.
contexts.residual-two-dictionary: Let X be a smooth genus-two curve over a field of characteristic different from2, A=Jac(X), and r₁,…,r₆ its geometric Weierstrass points. Use the fixed S6→Sp4(F2) identification of §8.1, rather than its outer-automorphism translate.
contexts.A5-modules: Let k⊂F₂-bar contain F4, choose A5≅SL2(F4), and let U be the tautological two-dimensional representation and U^σ its Frobenius-conjugate. Let V be the four-dimensional module defined over F2.
contexts.A5-automorphy: Let F⁺ be totally real and ρ̄:G_F⁺→GSp4(F2) have image S5(b) or A5(b), with every complex conjugation a nontrivial element of order2 in A5(b).
contexts.local-surface-data: For an abelian surface, ρ_{A,p}=H¹_et(A_bar,Q_p), so A[p] is the dual of its residual representation. At a good-reduction prime ℓ write the monic Frobenius characteristic polynomial Q_ℓ with constant term ℓ²; reciprocal Euler factors in the Magma files use a different polynomial normalization.
contexts.twisted-level-three: Let ρ̄:G_K→GSp4(F3) have multiplier ε̄⁻¹ over a characteristic-zero field K. Let P(ρ̄) be the twisted principally polarized surface moduli with a symplectic identification A[3]≅ρ̄∨ and a rational odd theta characteristic; M_w2(ρ̄) is its open genus-two Jacobian locus with a marked rational Weierstrass point.
contexts.local-three: Work over Q₃ with H¹ residual normalization ν=ε̄⁻¹; the finite-flat group representation is its dual of multiplier ε̄. Ordinary means an extension of an unramified rank2 quotient V̄ by its Cartier dual. Distinction refers to characteristic-zero unit roots, not residual characters.
contexts.two-three-switch: Let ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F3) have multiplier ε̄⁻¹, ordinary finite-flat dual at3 and unramified restriction at2. Use the smooth rational odd-theta space P(ρ̄), its dense Jacobian locus and local constancy of the finite torsion representations on p-adic neighborhoods.
contexts.modularity-switch-endpoints: All abelian-surface Galois representations use H¹. Modularity in the following general-type conclusions means a weight2 cuspidal GSp4 form with cuspidal GL4 transfer, and the corresponding H¹ L-function has the expected analytic continuation and functional equation. Source proof gates, including Arthur transfer, remain recorded in this extraction.
contexts.applications-counts: The statistical application refers to the paper fixed2024 LMFDB genus-two snapshot and to coefficient-box density in the specified generalized Weierstrass models. It is not a count of the current database and not a theorem about ordering all abelian surfaces by conductor.
contexts.potentially-abelian: Continuous p-adic Galois representations have finite dimension over Q_p-bar and are de Rham at all p-adic places. Potentially abelian means that restriction to some finite Galois extension has abelian image; finite up to twist means a character twist has finite image.
contexts.dyadic-polarized-lifting: Let O be the ring of integers of a finite K/Q₂ with residue field F. Let G₁/O be finite flat, killed by2, of rank16 and supplied with λ:G₁≅G₁∨ satisfying λ∨=−λ. Suppose an ordinary PPAV surface A₀/F has A₀[2]≅G₁ special fibre. At2 a skew self-duality is not by itself a strongly alternating polarization datum.
contexts.mod-two-realization: Let ρ̄:G_Q→Sp4(F2)=S6 be continuous and unramified at3, with nonidentity Frobenius at3. Assume a specified ordinary finite flat model W/Z₂ of ρ̄ exists and is isomorphic to its Cartier dual; ordinary means an extension of an étale group by a multiplicative group. The specified model, not only the generic representation, is part of the hypothesis.
contexts.conditional-Serre: Use the source regular-weight residual Serre assertion: for every relevant prime p and every absolutely irreducible ρ̄:G_Q→GSp4(F_p) of multiplier ε̄⁻¹ whose local-p semisimplification is a sum of characters, there is an ordinary cuspidal GSp4/Q form of REGULAR weight, level prime to p and central character absolute-value squared with residual representation ρ̄.
contexts.shared-imports: These are prerequisites imported by the BCGP25 programme (especially §§1.6,4–7,9–10) from existing atlas owners, including the ten-author infrastructure arXiv1812.09999. They are planned imports, not claims that BCGP25 reproves them or that they are implemented.
contexts.coefficient-rings: Let O be the p-adic coefficient DVR with residue field k, and Λ a complete Noetherian local O-algebra with residue field k.
contexts.VB-local: For a Hodge-type tower with fixed toroidal cone data Σ, choose an open flag neighborhood U_FL and its tower preimage U_{K^p,Σ}. Let F be an LB g-sheaf; VB_Σ(F)=colim_{K′_p}RΓ(K′_p,π_HT,Σ⁻¹F⊗^L_{π_HT,Σ⁻¹O_FL}O_U).
contexts.regular-descent: Let ρ:G_Q→GSp4(Q_p-bar) be continuous with multiplier ε⁻¹. Galois representations of RACSDC GL4 forms use the r_π normalization; GSp4 forms use ρ_π.
